issuer: the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA)
note: Read 2026-11-03 on the DVLA's own pages (dvla.gov.gh), rendered in a browser: they load their text by script, and a plain fetch gets only the page's shell, which is why the earlier reads found no age or term. Age: 18. Services, B1: a learner's licence for class A or B needs its holder to be 18 or above; B2: the driving licence follows compulsory training with a certified Driver Training Institution and the theory and in-traffic tests, for which the page sets no shortest period, so the youngest full holder is held at 18. Fee: GHS 642.25, the standard rate for a new driving licence (stages 1 and 2), class B, on the Fees and Charges page; its premium rates (GHS 903.25, 1,012.25 and 1,003.25) are faster services, not held. Whether that fee covers the first two years isn't stated. Term: 2 years. The DVLA's newsroom (27 August 2026, on the Road Traffic Regulations 2026, L.I. 2519): a driver's licence is expected to be renewed every two years; Services, B3: a renewal is by a sticker on the licence; MyJoyOnline (24 September 2026), reporting the DVLA's statement under L.I. 2519, adds that the card is replaced after six years. The text of L.I. 2519 itself wasn't reached. No identification card is the DVLA's (the Ghana Card is the National Identification Authority's).
